Amumu.escape: Look for an opening to engage when Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy are down. Amumu has no ability to create distance on his own, so knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, then follow with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
Amumu.teamfight: Spread out and fight in open terrain so Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy cannot hit multiple allies. Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only when your allies can follow, then chain into Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there is no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your team's main damage dealer to stop Amumu from approaching.
Amumu.build: Get tenacity or a way to remove crowd control early to prepare for being caught by Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy. Then build magic resistance, and avoid stacking health alone because of the max health based damage from Amumu W Despair.
Amumu.combo: From out of sight, start rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! early to build speed, then hit Amumu and knock him up. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. Use the ultimate's slow to keep Amumu in its area until the root triggers.
Amumu.fight: Dodge or bait out Amumu Q Bandage Toss and Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy before engaging. Amumu has no ability to create distance on his own, so knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and hold him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If you need health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a minion or monster, which restores more health than using it on a champion.
Amumu.phase: In the late game, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume’s sustain and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to engage or protect your allies.
Amumu.watch: Amumu Q Bandage Toss stuns you and can be followed by Amumu R Curse of the Sad Mummy, so manage your distance first. Use minions or jungle monsters as cover, since Bandage Toss stops at the first target it hits. When Amumu has his ultimate, spread out from your team and fight in open areas.

Elise.phase: Early on, watch out for Elise trying to get ahead with ganks and don't give her kills. As the game goes on, keep contributing with the sustain from Q Consume, R Absolute Zero, engages, and ally protection.
Elise.build: Build magic resistance first against Elise's main ability damage. Also consider armor for her basic attack damage, and tenacity if the stun from Elise E Cocoon is a problem.
Elise.combo: After Elise E Cocoon and E Rappel are down, build up Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! sufficiently from out of sight and hit her. While she is knocked up, cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times, then use the slow from Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold her until the root triggers.
Elise.escape: Right after Elise uses Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite is your chance to close the distance. Once you've confirmed that Elise E Cocoon and E Rappel are both down, counter by locking her down with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage.
Elise.fight: Nunu & Willump lack the damage to secure kills solo early, so fight when your allies can follow up. Close the distance right after Elise uses Q Neurotoxin / Venomous Bite, and engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! once Elise E Cocoon and E Rappel are both down.
Elise.laning: Get plenty of vision so Elise can't get kills with her early ganks, and don't push the lane recklessly while she is missing.
Elise.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance your allies can follow, knock the enemy up, then hold them with E Snowball Barrage and R Absolute Zero. If there is no good angle to engage, or Elise goes for your carry, activate R Absolute Zero in front of your carry to stop the engage.
Elise.watch: When health has decreased, Elise can look for a finishing blow by transforming with R Spider Form, so use the shield from Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero.

Graves.build: Graves' main damage is physical, so prioritize Plated Steelcaps and armor. Graves W Smoke Screen deals magic damage and is not blocked by armor, but armor is still the priority against him.
Graves.combo: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of vision, far from the lane, to build speed, then knock Graves up. While he is airborne, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with its slow until the root triggers. Graves can escape if his mobility is still available, so check whether he has used it before starting the combo.
Graves.escape: If only Graves E Quickdraw is down, he can still escape with Graves R Collateral Damage. Look for an opening before Graves R Collateral Damage comes back, and lock him down with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
Graves.fight: Counterattack or create distance while Graves reloads after firing two shots. His basic attacks are blocked by the first unit hit, so fight with minions or allies between you. Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! in open terrain where you have room to dodge the explosion from Graves Q End of the Line.
Graves.laning: Pressure the lane early to limit the time Graves has to build stacks, and focus on ganks and objectives over competing for farm.
Graves.phase: Graves grows stronger over time, putting you at a disadvantage, but Nunu & Willump can still engage and protect allies in the late game.
Graves.teamfight: From a distance where your allies can follow, knock Graves up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times, then cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If Graves tries to escape with a mobility ability, recast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to detonate it instead of waiting for its maximum damage. If there is no good engage angle, cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy engage.
Graves.watch: Graves Q End of the Line detonates immediately when it hits terrain, so do not fight with a wall behind you or in a narrow jungle path. If you are caught in Graves W Smoke Screen, leave it by the shortest route, then re-engage. Graves E Quickdraw and Graves R Collateral Damage are both mobility tools, so do not force an engage when only one is down.

Belveth.fight: Fight with your allies early, before Bel'Veth stacks up, but don't go deep alone because Nunu & Willump lack the damage to secure kills solo. After Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom ends, lock her down with the knockup from Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If you need health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume precisely on a minion or monster rather than a champion.
Belveth.phase: As the game goes on, Bel'Veth P Death in Lavender's permanent stacks put you at a disadvantage, so focus on engaging and protecting your allies in the late game.
Belveth.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Bel'Veth Q Void Surge and Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom. Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet's true damage cannot be mitigated by resistances, so build health as well. If slows are a problem, consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching.
Belveth.combo: From out of sight, roll in with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! to knock Bel'Veth up, then cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero, using its slow to hold her until E's root triggers. If Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom is active, interrupt it with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! or wait for it to end before dealing damage.
Belveth.escape: Dodge Bel'Veth W Above and Below; the moment Bel'Veth Q Void Surge is down is your opening to engage. Bel'Veth Q Void Surge has separate cooldowns for each direction, so aim Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage based on the direction she just dashed from. Since Bel'Veth Q Void Surge comes back quickly, chain your crowd control.
Belveth.laning: After a gank, use the Rift Scuttler to build up your snowball again and keep applying pressure. Bel'Veth is weak early, so steal large monsters and camps to slow her stacking.
Belveth.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and knock Bel'Veth up when your allies can follow, then hold her with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there's no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your carry to stop Bel'Veth from engaging. If an ally dies and drops Void Coral, retreat before Bel'Veth can pick it up, and delay the teamfight while she is transformed.
Belveth.watch: Bel'Veth W Above and Below slows and knocks you up, and can also create another cast of Bel'Veth Q Void Surge, so sidestep when she closes in. Don't pour damage into Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom while it is active; wait for it to end or interrupt it with the knockup from Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! When your health is low, watch out for the missing health based damage from Bel'Veth E Royal Maelstrom and Bel'Veth R Endless Banquet.

Ivern.combo: After Ivern Q Rootcaller is down and E Triggerseed has burst, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! built from a distance. Then throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and cast R Absolute Zero to hold him with its slow until the root triggers. If Ivern R Daisy! is blocking the way, do not throw your snowball at an opponent behind Daisy.
Ivern.build: Prioritize tenacity because it is dangerous when allies follow up on Ivern's roots and knockups. He also has many slows, so Mercury's Treads with Unflinching is useful. If you need more resistance, build magic resistance against the magic damage from Ivern Q Rootcaller, W Brushmaker, and E Triggerseed.
Ivern.escape: The moment after Ivern Q Rootcaller is down is your window to engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! Do not immediately engage a target affected by Ivern E Triggerseed; go in after the shield bursts. Nunu & Willump has no ability to escape on his own, so do not give up your distance while Ivern's crowd control is available.
Ivern.fight: After making Ivern use Q Rootcaller, close the gap with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! If a target already has Ivern E Triggerseed on them, wait for the shield to burst before going in, then lock them down with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Focus first on catching an ally Ivern shields rather than chasing Ivern deep.
Ivern.laning: Warding Ivern's jungle early lets you track his route as he comes to harvest camps. Do not casually walk beside brush that suddenly appears from Ivern W Brushmaker.
Ivern.phase: Even in the late game, Nunu & Willump can contribute by engaging with a snowball and protecting allies.
Ivern.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! when your allies can follow, and target anyone affected by Ivern E Triggerseed after the shield bursts. If there is no good engage angle, cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy from engaging. Reposition so Ivern R Daisy! cannot hit you repeatedly.
Ivern.watch: If you are rooted by Ivern Q Rootcaller, Ivern's allies can dash in, so keep a minion or terrain between you before he fires it. Do not engage a target affected by Ivern E Triggerseed until the shield bursts and leaves a slow. If Ivern R Daisy! starts hitting you, reposition to avoid the knockup from her consecutive attacks.

Brand.laning: Don't start rolling your snowball where Brand can see you; begin from out of sight, away from lane. Brand E Conflagration can spread around burning minions, so don't engage right next to a burning wave and your allies.
Brand.build: Brand's main damage is magic, and Brand P Blaze deals damage based on your max health, so build magic resistance first. Account for the slow from Brand R Pyroclasm and the self-slow while rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!; if you need slow resistance, consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching.
Brand.combo: From out of sight, build up Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and knock Brand up. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero, using its slow to keep Brand in the area until the root triggers. If Brand tries to escape, end Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early to detonate it.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility, so close the distance as soon as Brand W Pillar of Flame is down. If a burn is active, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear or wait until the burn ends before engaging. Once you're close, block his escape with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
Brand.fight: Look to engage just after Brand W Pillar of Flame is down. From out of sight, start rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! early to build speed, and if Brand's body is burning, approach while avoiding the stun from Brand Q Sear. Nunu & Willump's main magic damage works well against Brand's low magic resistance.
Brand.phase: In the mid and late game, the healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume and the burst from Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero both increase; in the late game, focus on engaging and protecting allies.
Brand.teamfight: Spread out from allies to limit the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces from Brand R Pyroclasm, and don't stand beside a burning ally. When your allies can follow, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there is no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your carry to stop the enemy team from engaging.
Brand.watch: After Brand P Blaze applies, follow-up hits from other abilities build stacks and cause an explosion, so focus on dodging his first ability, Brand Q Sear or Brand W Pillar of Flame. While you are burning, Brand Q Sear stuns, so move out of the projectile's path or hide behind minions. When you see Brand R Pyroclasm being cast, spread out from your allies to reduce its bouncing damage.

Fiddlesticks.fight: Build up Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance to engage. When Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest starts, interrupt it with a knock-up or the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Since Fiddlesticks' fear and silence make it difficult to escape, watch your spacing and engage when your allies can follow up.
Fiddlesticks.build: Prioritize tenacity so Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and Fiddlesticks E Reap do not keep you locked down while his ultimate hits. Consider Mercury's Treads with Unflinching, and build magic resistance rather than armor to reduce his damage.
Fiddlesticks.combo: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! sufficiently from out of vision and hit the target, then throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times while the target is airborne. Follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold them with its slow until the root triggers and aim for the explosion damage. If you need to interrupt Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest, time your knockup or root to its channel.
Fiddlesticks.escape: Once Fiddlesticks Q Terrify and the silence from Fiddlesticks E Reap are down, the risk of being locked down is lower. Knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and root him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage to stop his escape.
Fiddlesticks.laning: While Fiddlesticks is out of sight, keep the brush behind the lane warded, and do not walk past a stationary Fiddlesticks P A Harmless Scarecrow without checking it. After a gank, go through the Rift Scuttler area, build your snowball again, and look for another opening.
Fiddlesticks.phase: In the late game, use the sustain from Nunu & Willump Q Consume and the power of Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to engage or protect your allies.
Fiddlesticks.teamfight: Secure vision in the brush and approaches near objectives, and spread out so Fiddlesticks' area abilities do not hit you together. When your allies can follow, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and interrupt Fiddlesticks W Bountiful Harvest or Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm while they channel. If there is no good engage angle, cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop Fiddlesticks from engaging.
Fiddlesticks.watch: Fiddlesticks R Crowstorm moves after channeling and deals area damage. If you see the cast, interrupt it with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!; if you cannot, move out of range. When Fiddlesticks has been out of sight for a while, watch for ambushes from brush, and do not group up in narrow paths without vision.

LeeSin.watch: Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will can also be used to engage by ward-hopping over walls, so keep your distance from walls without vision. In teamfights, watch which way Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage will send you and spread out from your allies.
LeeSin.build: Build armor first to mitigate the physical damage from Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike and Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage. If the slow from Lee Sin E Tempest / Cripple is troublesome, get slow resistance with Mercury's Treads and Unflinching to help engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and root with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
LeeSin.combo: Before Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike comes back up, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from far away to build speed, then collide with him and knock him up. Follow with three throws of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with the slow until the root triggers. If Lee Sin still has a mobility ability available, he can escape, so check for it before engaging.
LeeSin.escape: Engage while Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike has missed or cannot be used again. If Lee Sin W Safeguard / Iron Will is also still available, do not go in just because one ability is down.
LeeSin.fight: If you encounter Lee Sin in the jungle early, avoid dueling him and gain an advantage through ganks and objectives. Look for Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike to miss or be unavailable to use again, then knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and hold him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If health has decreased, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a jungle monster to recover.
LeeSin.laning: After a gank, you can pass by the Rift Scuttler to build the snowball again and repeat. On lanes where you expect a Lee Sin gank, stand behind minions to block the straight-line angle for Lee Sin Q Sonic Wave / Resonating Strike.
LeeSin.phase: In the late game, Nunu & Willump handles engages and protects allies while Lee Sin's power falls off.
LeeSin.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only when allies are within follow-up range, knock Lee Sin up, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there is no opening to engage, use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to stop Lee Sin from engaging. Immediately before a team fight, create distance so you do not collide with allies knocked back by Lee Sin R Dragon's Rage.

Zac.phase: Nunu & Willump still has an engage and ally-protection role in the late game, but the available information isn't enough to determine which champion has the advantage at each stage against Zac.
Zac.build: Against the slows from Zac Q Stretching Strikes and Zac R Let's Bounce!, prioritize Mercury's Treads and use Unflinching alongside them. Build magic resistance against the damage from Zac Q Stretching Strikes, Zac W Unstable Matter, and Zac E Elastic Slingshot. Since Zac W Unstable Matter deals damage based on your maximum health, avoid stacking health alone.
Zac.combo: If Zac E Elastic Slingshot is down, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from far away and hit him; while he’s airborne, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Then use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to slow him and keep him in range until the delayed root triggers. If Zac is charging Zac E Elastic Slingshot, first look for an angle to interrupt it with the knockup from Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!.
Zac.escape: The moment after you bait out Zac E Elastic Slingshot is your opportunity to engage with Nunu & Willump. Knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and follow with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If Zac Q Stretching Strikes catches you with crowd control first, you have no ability to escape on your own, so check your distance before engaging.
Zac.fight: Right after Zac uses Zac E Elastic Slingshot, close the gap with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and catch him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. During the fight, step on the blobs from Zac P Cell Division to stop his healing. If you need healing from Nunu & Willump Q Consume, aim carefully at a minion or monster. Engage when your allies can follow up instead of trying to secure a kill alone.
Zac.laning: If you start rolling close to the enemy, the snowball is easy to dodge, so make sure you have enough distance for the engage. After a gank, roll the Rift Scuttler to build up the snowball again and look for another gank.
Zac.teamfight: After responding to Zac E Elastic Slingshot’s engage, create distance from your allies as you fight to avoid the damage from Zac W Unstable Matter. When engaging with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, keep within range for your allies to follow up. If there’s no good angle to engage, or Zac goes after your allied carry, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of the carry to stop him.
Zac.watch: Zac E Elastic Slingshot charges before dashing in to knock you up, so if you see him charging behind a wall, interrupt it with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! If Zac Q Stretching Strikes slows and knocks you up, Nunu & Willump has no ability to escape and can easily be hit again, so keep your distance. Zac W Unstable Matter deals damage based on your maximum health, so don’t stay close for an extended fight.

Briar.build: Briar's main damage is physical, so build armor first. Managing your distance to avoid Briar Q Head Rush is also important because it reduces your armor. If Briar's healing becomes a problem in a prolonged duel, consider anti-heal after building resistances.
Briar.combo: After Briar's mobility ability is down, start rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! early from out of sight to build speed and land the knockup. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and activate R Absolute Zero, using its slow to hold her until the root triggers. If Briar tries to leave the area, don't wait for maximum damage; reactivate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to detonate it.
Briar.escape: Don't engage just because Briar Q Head Rush is down. Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack also lets her dash, so confirm both abilities have been used, and look especially for a window before Briar R Certain Death comes back. Then hold her with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage.
Briar.fight: Briar has several ways to lock you down, and Nunu & Willump has no ability to escape on his own, so keep your distance and fight with allies. When Briar charges E Chilling Scream, hit her with a Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! you've already rolled to stop her healing and prevent the wall stun. If you need health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume precisely on a minion or monster rather than a champion.
Briar.laning: Briar has a strong early gank presence, so don't stay long in the middle of a lane without vision. Push the lane to secure vision, then punish any reckless engage. Nunu & Willump lack the damage to secure kills solo, so look for opportunities where allies can follow up.
Briar.phase: In the mid and late game, the sustain from Nunu & Willump Q Consume and the burst from R Absolute Zero increase; even in the late game, focus on engaging and protecting allies.
Briar.teamfight: While Briar W Blood Frenzy / Snack Attack is active, she targets the nearest enemy, so have Nunu & Willump stand at the front to block her path to your damage dealers. Briar R Certain Death's bloodstone also makes the first champion it hits her prey, so set up a frontline and group around the marked ally to counter-engage. If there is no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your carry to stop Briar from engaging.
Briar.watch: Briar Q Head Rush dashes in, stuns, and reduces your armor, so don't stay in range and fight for long. When Briar E Chilling Scream starts charging, look for a chance to interrupt it with the knockup from Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! A fully charged scream stuns enemies who hit a wall, so don't fight with your back to one.

Ekko.build: Get tenacity early so you aren't caught by Ekko W Parallel Convergence's stun and hit by his combo. Then build magic resistance against Ekko's magic damage. If you also need slow resistance, consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching.
Ekko.combo: From out of sight, start rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! early and knock Ekko up. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then use the slow from Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him until the root triggers. If Ekko tries to escape with Ekko R Chronobreak, reactivate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to detonate it instead of waiting for maximum damage.
Ekko.escape: The moment Ekko E Phase Dive is down is your chance to hit him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If only Ekko E Phase Dive is down, he can still survive with Ekko R Chronobreak, so don't go deep. Look for a window when both Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak are down.
Ekko.fight: Right after Ekko closes in with E Phase Dive, his mobility ability is down, so hold him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! or Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, don't chase deep just because he is low. It's safer to fight in earnest after Ekko W Parallel Convergence and Ekko R Chronobreak have been used.
Ekko.phase: Even in the late game, Nunu & Willump's role is to engage and protect allies; avoid overcommitting to chase when Ekko's afterimage is visible.
Ekko.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance your allies can follow. If Ekko uses Ekko E Phase Dive to reach an ally, lock him down with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! or Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and pressure him to use Ekko R Chronobreak. If there is no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your carry to stop Ekko from engaging.
Ekko.watch: When you see the signal for Ekko W Parallel Convergence, stay out of the marked area to avoid the stun and shield. Also sidestep the return path of Ekko Q Timewinder. If Ekko's afterimage is visible, Ekko R Chronobreak is ready, so don't overcommit to chasing him even if he looks low.

Evelynn.build: Build magic resistance first against Evelynn's main damage. Evelynn W Allure reduces magic resistance, and Evelynn E Whiplash deals damage based on max health, so instead of stacking health alone, also get movement speed to retreat before the mark matures.
Evelynn.combo: From out of sight, start rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! early and knock Evelynn up, then cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Follow by activating Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero and using its slow to hold her until the root triggers, but detonate R early if Evelynn tries to escape with a mobility ability.
Evelynn.escape: If only Evelynn E Whiplash is down, Evelynn can still escape with R Last Caress, so don't force an engage. Look for a chance to hold her with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back and before the mark from Evelynn W Allure matures.
Evelynn.fight: Create distance before the mark from Evelynn W Allure matures. You can reveal a stealthed Evelynn by throwing Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage along her expected approach path. Before Evelynn R Last Caress comes back, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance your allies can fight alongside you.
Evelynn.phase: Even in the late game, Nunu & Willump's role is to engage and protect allies, but the information provided is not enough to determine which of the two champions is stronger.
Evelynn.teamfight: Evelynn may go for your backline damage dealers, so fight within your team's vision and save Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage to hold her. If there is no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your damage dealers to stop Evelynn from approaching.
Evelynn.watch: If you see a mark from Evelynn W Allure, Evelynn is nearby preparing a charm, so retreat before the mark matures and alert your allies.

Gragas.build: Consider Mercury's Treads first to deal with slows, and pair them with Unflinching for slow resistance. Build magic resistance rather than armor against Gragas Q Barrel Roll, W Drunken Rage, and E Body Slam. Gragas W Drunken Rage deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid choices that add a large amount of health alone.
Gragas.combo: Once Gragas E Body Slam is down, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! built out of sight. Then throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and cast R Absolute Zero to hold him with its slow until the root triggers. If Gragas has R Explosive Cask available to push you out of range, do not fixate on channeling Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero for its full duration.
Gragas.escape: The window to engage is right after you make Gragas use E Body Slam. Close the gap then with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage to look for a root. If Gragas E Body Slam hits you, move out of Gragas Q Barrel Roll's radius before trying to retaliate.
Gragas.fight: Do not pour damage into Gragas while he drinks with W Drunken Rage; attack after the effect ends. Once Gragas E Body Slam is down, close the gap with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and lock him down with E Snowball Barrage. A deep chase risks getting hit by Gragas E Body Slam again, so only commit when you can secure the kill.
Gragas.phase: If you hold your formation and endure the early and mid-game objective fights, Gragas' sustained damage falls off in the late game, making him easier to deal with.
Gragas.teamfight: Do not leave your allied backline alone within range of Gragas E Body Slam, and avoid narrow paths and brush without vision. Once Gragas E Body Slam is down and your allies can follow, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and chain into E Snowball Barrage and R Absolute Zero. If there is no good engage angle, cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop Gragas from engaging.
Gragas.watch: When you see Gragas Q Barrel Roll, leave its radius before it explodes. Keep your distance near the barrel so you do not also get hit by Gragas E Body Slam. When Gragas has Gragas R Explosive Cask available, do not stand with an enemy turret or the enemy team behind you.

Hecarim.build: Prioritize armor against Hecarim's main damage from Hecarim Q Rampage and Hecarim E Devastating Charge. Also account for Hecarim W Spirit of Dread and Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows dealing magic damage, which armor cannot block.
Hecarim.combo: After Hecarim's mobility is down, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of vision and knock him up. Then hit him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with its slow until the root triggers. If Hecarim tries to leave the area, end Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early to detonate it.
Hecarim.escape: Do not engage just because Hecarim E Devastating Charge is down. Hecarim can also escape with Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows, so look for an opening especially before that ability comes back, and use Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage to lock him down.
Hecarim.fight: If Hecarim gets on you, Nunu & Willump has no ability to escape on his own, so manage your distance first. During a fight, disrupt his movement with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! or Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage to reduce Hecarim's access and damage.
Hecarim.phase: Even in the late game, Nunu & Willump can contribute by engaging with a snowball or protecting allies.
Hecarim.teamfight: Spread out from your allies so Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows does not catch several of you. If your allies are close enough to follow, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and knock him up, then disrupt Hecarim's movement with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there is no good engage angle, cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop Hecarim from engaging.
Hecarim.watch: Hecarim E Devastating Charge deals more damage and knocks you back farther the farther he runs. If Hecarim turns toward the opposite direction and starts running, break vision or move toward your allies. Hecarim R Onslaught of Shadows can fear several people at once, so spread out from your allies.

JarvanIV.build: Since basic attacks and attack speed are central to damage output, an option that reduces attack speed is also effective.
JarvanIV.combo: Then throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and cast R Absolute Zero, holding the target with its slow until the root triggers.
JarvanIV.fight: If you are low on health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a minion or monster to heal.
JarvanIV.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only when your allies can follow, then chain into E Snowball Barrage and R Absolute Zero after the knockup.

Jax.build: Jax's damage relies on basic attacks and attack speed, so prioritize an attack speed slow. Jax Q Leap Strike deals physical damage, while Jax W Empower and Jax E Counter Strike deal magic damage, so build both armor and magic resistance. Jax E Counter Strike deals damage based on maximum health, so avoid choices that add a large amount of health alone.
Jax.combo: After Jax Q Leap Strike and Jax E Counter Strike are down, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of vision, collide with him, and knock him up. During that time, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and cast Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with its slow until the root triggers.
Jax.escape: The moment after you make Jax use Q Leap Strike is your window to close the gap with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If Jax E Counter Strike is also down, avoid the stun and then engage. If Counter Strike is still active, move out of stun range first.
Jax.fight: While Jax E Counter Strike is active, stop basic attacking and wait outside stun range for its duration to end. After Jax Q Leap Strike or Jax E Counter Strike is down, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! alongside your allies and pressure him with your abilities.
Jax.laning: Start rolling your snowball out of sight, far from the lane.
Jax.phase: In the mid-to-late game, use the sustain from Nunu & Willump Q Consume and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to engage or protect your allies.
Jax.teamfight: When Jax engages with Jax E Counter Strike active, do not group up with your allies; wait for the area stun to end. Immediately afterward, lock him down with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, and use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to stop his engage or apply more slow.
Jax.watch: While Jax E Counter Strike is active, do not use basic attacks empowered by Nunu & Willump P Call of the Freljord. Jax can use Jax Q Leap Strike to close in and aim for E Counter Strike's area stun, so when Counter Strike is active, move out of stun range and wait for it to end.

Karthus.build: Karthus Q Lay Waste, Karthus E Defile, and Karthus R Requiem all deal magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance. If slows often stop you from engaging, consider Mercury's Treads with Unflinching. Even with resistance, avoiding Karthus W Wall of Pain and quickly leaving Karthus E Defile's area come first.
Karthus.combo: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from far away until it is large enough, then knock Karthus up. While he is airborne, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and keep him close with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero's slow until the root triggers.
Karthus.escape: If Karthus W Wall of Pain has been placed, engage by going around the wall instead of crossing it. Once close, use Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage's root to stop him from escaping.
Karthus.fight: Karthus has no way to create distance, so charge Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of vision and engage. After killing him, reposition immediately to avoid Karthus P Death Defied.
Karthus.laning: Your damage is too low to secure kills alone, so engage within range of allied follow-up and focus on ganks and objectives over competing for farm.
Karthus.phase: In the late game, Nunu & Willump handles engages and protects allies. After killing Karthus, reposition to avoid Karthus P Death Defied.
Karthus.teamfight: When allies can follow up, knock up the target with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, then chain Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage into Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. Karthus continues dealing damage after death, so move away from his corpse as soon as he is killed. If there is no opening to engage, use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to stop enemies from approaching.
Karthus.watch: Karthus Q Lay Waste deals heavy damage if it hits you alone, so watch for the blast indicator and dodge. If possible, stand on top of an ally or minion. Karthus W Wall of Pain slows and reduces magic resistance, so go around the wall. Even after Karthus is killed, Karthus P Death Defied lets him keep using abilities, so move away from his corpse immediately. After a fight, save enough health to survive Karthus R Requiem.

MasterYi.build: Use health to withstand the true damage from Master Yi E Wuju Style. An attack speed reduction can also slow both his basic attacks and the cooldown reduction on Master Yi Q Alpha Strike.
MasterYi.combo: As soon as Master Yi Q Alpha Strike ends, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! rolled from far away. If Master Yi R Highlander is active, focus on landing the knock-up and root instead of relying on slows.
MasterYi.escape: The moment after Master Yi Q Alpha Strike is down is your chance to engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. While Master Yi R Highlander is active, do not try to create distance with slows; use immobilizing crowd control or retreat around terrain.
MasterYi.fight: As Master Yi lands after using Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and prepare to root him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If Master Yi activates Master Yi W Meditate, interrupt the channel with a knock-up or root you have saved.
MasterYi.laning: Master Yi is weak at jungling and ganking early, so focus on gaining an advantage through ganks and early objectives instead of competing for farm.
MasterYi.phase: Master Yi is weak at jungling and ganking early, so once you have Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, hurry to make plays with ganks and objectives. Master Yi gets stronger as the game goes on, so in the late game use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to protect allies and stop engages.
MasterYi.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only when allies are within follow-up range, and watch for Master Yi Q Alpha Strike to end before layering a knock-up and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage's root. If Master Yi gets the first takedown, he can immediately stick to his next target, so do not leave an ally alone to face him. If there is no opening to engage, use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to stop the engage.
MasterYi.watch: Master Yi can be targeted while casting Master Yi Q Alpha Strike, so aim for him as soon as he lands. When Master Yi R Highlander is active, slows do not work, and Master Yi E Wuju Style adds true damage to his basic attacks, so do not stay close and fight for long.

MonkeyKing.build: Build armor first against Wukong's main damage, and consider an attack speed reduction effect to take fewer basic attacks. Wukong Q Crushing Blow reduces armor and Wukong R Cyclone deals damage based on maximum health, so be careful about stacking health alone. Armor cannot block the magic damage from Wukong E Nimbus Strike.
MonkeyKing.combo: After confirming Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of vision and knock up the real Wukong. Follow with three throws of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with its slow until the root triggers. If Wukong is about to leave the area, end Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early to detonate it.
MonkeyKing.escape: Wukong W Warrior Trickster and Wukong E Nimbus Strike are both mobility tools, so do not rush in when only one is down. In particular, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage before Wukong W Warrior Trickster comes back up. If Wukong R Cyclone has also just been fully expended, that is an opportunity to force an objective or fight.
MonkeyKing.fight: Nunu & Willump's magic damage is effective against Wukong's low magic resistance, so look for short trades. If you stay close for too long, Wukong P Stone Skin's armor and healing build up, so fight by knocking him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, landing Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then backing off. After Wukong W Warrior Trickster is down, identify the real Wukong and engage again.
MonkeyKing.laning: You can trade back with magic damage when Wukong gets close, but do not fight for long within Wukong E Nimbus Strike's range. If you need sustain, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume accurately on a minion or monster.
MonkeyKing.phase: In the mid to late game, Nunu & Willump Q Consume's sustain and R Absolute Zero's burst improve, and Nunu & Willump still handles engages and protects allies in the late game.
MonkeyKing.teamfight: When allies can follow up, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and chain into Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there is no opening to engage, use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to stop Wukong from engaging.
MonkeyKing.watch: Wukong E Nimbus Strike is a targeted dash, so keep your distance outside its range. When Wukong W Warrior Trickster creates a clone, do not use Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! or Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage on the stationary clone; watch the direction the real Wukong is heading.

Nidalee.build: Nidalee's main damage is magic damage, so build magic resistance first. Dodging spears comes first; there is no basis in the provided information for choosing a specific item.
Nidalee.combo: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of vision to knock Nidalee up, then throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold her with its slow until E's delayed root triggers. If Nidalee is about to escape, end R early to detonate it.
Nidalee.escape: The moment after you make Nidalee use W Pounce is your chance to close the distance. Chain Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! into Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage to hold her while her mobility is down. Nidalee has no crowd control, so there is no need to wait for her crowd control to be down.
Nidalee.fight: Nunu & Willump's solo damage is low early, so start fights within range of allied follow-up. Right after Nidalee uses Nidalee W Pounce, take advantage of her mobility being down: knock her up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and hold her with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
Nidalee.laning: Check for Nidalee W Bushwhack in river and jungle entrances with a Control Ward or Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage before entering. Focus on ganks and objectives over competing for farm.
Nidalee.phase: In the late game, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume's healing and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to engage or protect allies.
Nidalee.teamfight: Watch where Nidalee steps out to throw Nidalee Q Javelin Toss, and engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! when allies can follow up. Layer the slow from Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage to hold Nidalee. If there is no opening to engage, activate R in front of an allied carry to stop Nidalee from engaging.
Nidalee.watch: Nidalee Q Javelin Toss deals more damage the farther away it hits from, so be especially careful to dodge its path when Nidalee is far away. Watch for Nidalee W Bushwhack in jungle entrances and along the river. If you are hit by a spear or trap, save Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage for the moment Nidalee uses Nidalee W Pounce to enter.

Nocturne.build: Build armor first against Nocturne’s main damage from Nocturne P Umbra Blades, Nocturne Q Duskbringer, and Nocturne R Paranoia. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror, but the information provided isn’t enough to determine the purchase order for specific items or additional resistance.
Nocturne.combo: When there is no shield, knock the target up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! built up outside vision, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then apply a slow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero.
Nocturne.escape: If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror tethers to you, create distance first to break it, then engage again once the fear threat is gone.
Nocturne.fight: Roll the snowball early from outside vision to build speed, then make contact from within range for your allies to follow up. Nunu & Willump lacks the damage to secure kills alone early, so fight alongside your allies.
Nocturne.laning: Maintain vision in the river and at jungle entrances, and position yourself so you can fall back toward your allies before Nocturne R Paranoia activates. If you need health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume precisely on a minion or monster.
Nocturne.phase: Late game, Nunu & Willump handles engages and protects allies, and the information provided isn’t enough to determine which side is stronger overall.
Nocturne.teamfight: When Nocturne R Paranoia darkens the screen, stay close to your allies so no one is isolated. If Nocturne engages on your allied carry, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero beneath them to stop his engage with slows and a shield. When there’s an opportunity to attack, knock the target up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from within range for your allies to follow up, then chain Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage into Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero.
Nocturne.watch: If Nocturne Q Duskbringer hits you, Nocturne can quickly run along its trail, so don’t flee in a straight line; turn toward your allies or turret. If Nocturne E Unspeakable Horror tethers to you, create distance to break it before the fear triggers. Be careful not to use the knockup from Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! right away while Nocturne W Shroud of Darkness is active.

Poppy.build: Build armor first against Poppy Q Hammer Shock, E Heroic Charge, and R Keeper's Verdict. Poppy Q Hammer Shock deals damage based on your max health, so be cautious about stacking health alone. If the enemy team has many slows, take Mercury's Treads and Unflinching for slow resistance to build Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! speed faster.
Poppy.combo: After Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends and she uses E Heroic Charge, knock her up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! built out of sight. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate R Absolute Zero to keep her slowed until the root triggers. If Poppy tries to leave the area, end Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early to detonate it.
Poppy.escape: Right after Poppy uses E Heroic Charge is Nunu & Willump's window to engage. Confirm that Poppy W Steadfast Presence has also ended, then approach with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! If Poppy is charging R Keeper's Verdict, first move sideways out of its path.
Poppy.fight: While Poppy W Steadfast Presence is active, don't engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!; wait for its duration to end. Right after Poppy uses E Heroic Charge, close the distance and catch her with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage. Even if Poppy is low on health, wait until you can finish her reliably, since her armor and magic resistance increase.
Poppy.laning: On a lane with Poppy, avoid paths that leave you with your back to a wall or narrow passage, and engage after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends. After a gank, roll the Rift Scuttler to build another snowball and look for repeat ganks.
Poppy.phase: In the mid to late game, Nunu & Willump Q Consume provides more sustain and R Absolute Zero deals more burst damage. Continue to engage and protect allies in the late game.
Poppy.teamfight: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only from a distance your allies can follow up from, and engage after Poppy W Steadfast Presence ends. If there's no opening to engage or Poppy goes for an allied carry, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of the carry to block her approach.
Poppy.watch: Poppy E Heroic Charge stuns you if it hits a wall, so stand in open space instead of with your back to a wall. If Poppy Q Hammer Shock hits you on the first strike, immediately walk out of the remaining zone. When Poppy charges R Keeper's Verdict, move sideways out of its path.

Rammus.build: Build magic resistance first against Rammus's main damage. Nunu & Willump have no ability to escape on their own, so you can prioritize tenacity if you keep getting locked down by crowd control. Consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching if slows are a problem.
Rammus.combo: While Rammus is airborne, cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep him slowed until the root triggers. If you're within range of Rammus E Frenzying Taunt, don't start channeling Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero because he can interrupt it.
Rammus.escape: If Rammus E Frenzying Taunt is also down, it's a good time to follow up with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If you've already been taunted, you can't move or use abilities until it ends.
Rammus.fight: When Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, don't hit him with empowered basic attacks; briefly back off. After it ends, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and focus your damage. You have a hard time securing kills alone, so go in when an ally can attack with you.
Rammus.laning: Keep a minion wave between you and Rammus Q Powerball's approach, and don't start a fight within Rammus E Frenzying Taunt range. After a gank, roll the Rift Scuttler to build another snowball for a repeat gank.
Rammus.phase: In the late game, Nunu & Willump still engage with allies or protect them with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero.
Rammus.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance your allies can follow up from. If Rammus W Defensive Ball Curl is active, target someone else instead of Rammus. If Rammus Q Powerball goes for an allied carry, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of the carry to block his engage. Keep your distance so you don't start channeling within range of Rammus E Frenzying Taunt.
Rammus.watch: When you see Rammus Q Powerball, stand behind a minion wave and block his approach before he collides with you. Rammus E Frenzying Taunt prevents movement and ability use, so fight outside its range. Rammus R Soaring Slam after rolling at max speed has a wider area than expected, so move well clear and leave the landing area immediately.

RekSai.build: Build armor first against Rek'Sai's main damage. Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel deals true damage that armor can't reduce, so you also need health, but avoid stacking health alone because Rek'Sai R Void Rush deals damage based on your max health. If you can reduce her attack speed, it helps reduce her basic attack damage from Rek'Sai Q Queen's Wrath / Prey Seeker.
RekSai.combo: Look for an opening after the knockup from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel, and Rek'Sai R Void Rush are down. Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from out of sight ahead of time, knock her up, then cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to slow her until the root triggers.
RekSai.escape: Go in after dodging the knockup from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow and once both Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel and R Void Rush are down. In particular, before Rek'Sai R Void Rush becomes available again, you have a chance to catch her with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage.
RekSai.fight: Dodge the knockup from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, then engage when your allies can fight with you. If only Rek'Sai E Furious Bite / Tunnel is down, she can still escape with R Void Rush, so don't rush the chase. If you're low on health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a monster to heal.
RekSai.laning: Don't move alone through areas without vision, so you don't give up a kill to Rek'Sai's early ganks. Walk over visible tunnel entrances to destroy them. Focus on ganks and objectives over competing for farm.
RekSai.phase: Rek'Sai's early ganks are dangerous, so avoid giving up kills and buy time. In the mid to late game, Nunu & Willump Q Consume provides more sustain and R Absolute Zero deals more damage. Continue to engage and protect allies in the late game.
RekSai.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance your allies can follow up from, and overlap Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If Rek'Sai can escape with E Furious Bite / Tunnel or R Void Rush, consider ending Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early. If there's no opening to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to block Rek'Sai's engage.
RekSai.watch: When Rek'Sai is Burrowed, watch out for the knockup from Rek'Sai W Burrow / Un-burrow, and move toward open space, away from walls and narrow paths. Even after Rek'Sai closes the distance with E Furious Bite / Tunnel, she can go in again with R Void Rush. Immediately after Rek'Sai damages you, stay close to allies in case she uses R Void Rush.

Rengar.build: Build armor first against the main damage from Rengar Q Savagery, E Bola Strike, and R Thrill of the Hunt. Armor won't block the magic damage from Rengar W Battle Roar, and the effect of your armor is reduced while Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt lowers your resistances.
Rengar.combo: If Rengar W Battle Roar is down, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! built out of sight, then cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep him slowed until the root triggers. If Rengar cleanses the crowd control and tries to leave the area, end R early to detonate it.
Rengar.escape: Engage after dodging Rengar E Bola Strike or letting it pass. If Rengar W Battle Roar is also down and his resource bar is empty, he has no ability to create distance on his own, giving you a chance to catch him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage.
Rengar.fight: Trade when Rengar's resource bar is empty, and after confirming that he has used W Battle Roar, catch him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage. Your early damage is low on your own, so engage from a distance your allies can follow up from.
Rengar.laning: When Rengar is out of sight, avoid paths next to bushes and use Control Wards to secure vision along his approach routes. After a gank, roll the Rift Scuttler to build another snowball and look for repeat ganks.
Rengar.phase: In the mid to late game, Nunu & Willump continue to contribute with healing, teamfight engages, and ally protection.
Rengar.teamfight: Keep your formation so the back line doesn't move ahead of the front line, and stay with allies when Rengar engages with R Thrill of the Hunt so you can detect him early. After Rengar W Battle Roar is down, catch him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage. If there's no opening to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to protect them with its shield and slow and block Rengar's engage.
Rengar.watch: Rengar P Unseen Predator lets him leap from bushes and prepare an empowered ability, so when Rengar is out of sight, avoid paths next to bushes and use Control Wards for vision. While Rengar R Thrill of the Hunt is active, don't walk alone while injured; stay with allies so your detection ranges overlap. If Rengar's resource bar is full, watch out for the root from empowered E Bola Strike and the crowd control cleanse from empowered W Battle Roar.

Sejuani.build: Nunu & Willump have a hard time escaping on their own when caught by Sejuani Q Arctic Assault, E Permafrost, or R Glacial Prison, so consider tenacity first. Build magic resistance against Sejuani's main damage, but remember it won't block damage from Sejuani W Winter's Wrath. If there are many slows, Mercury's Treads and Unflinching also help when rolling Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!.
Sejuani.combo: After Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! ahead of time from out of sight and hit her, then cast E Snowball Barrage three times while she's airborne. Follow by activating Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep her slowed until the root from E Snowball Barrage triggers. Don't activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero on its own when Sejuani can escape with Q Arctic Assault.
Sejuani.escape: Right after Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down is your window to go in with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! After Sejuani E Permafrost stuns once, its stacks cannot build again for a short time, but immediately create distance after the stun to avoid Sejuani's first basic attack. If Sejuani Q Arctic Assault and R Glacial Prison are still available, keep your distance because Nunu & Willump can't escape on their own once caught.
Sejuani.fight: Right after you bait Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is an opportunity to engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! If Sejuani P Fury of the North is active, she is immune to slows, so damage her first to remove the armor, then catch her with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. If you need to heal with Nunu & Willump Q Consume, aim carefully at a minion or monster instead of a champion.
Sejuani.laning: If Sejuani Q Arctic Assault is down, use that window to look for ganks and objectives. Both champions have low early damage, so gain an advantage through ganks and objectives with allies instead of trying to secure kills alone.
Sejuani.phase: In the late game, Sejuani lasts longer and catches your allies as she builds health and defensive stats, but Nunu & Willump also gain sustain from Q Consume and burst damage from R Absolute Zero, and can engage and protect allies.
Sejuani.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only from a distance your allies can follow up from, then follow the knockup with E Snowball Barrage and R Absolute Zero. Don't go deep alone because Sejuani can catch you with Q Arctic Assault or R Glacial Prison. If there's no opening to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to block Sejuani's engage.
Sejuani.watch: Sejuani Q Arctic Assault dashes in and knocks you up, while Sejuani R Glacial Prison stuns, so move sideways to dodge when you see their windups. If Sejuani W Winter's Wrath hits you with its first strike, get out of range before the second. Sejuani E Permafrost stacks can also build from her melee allies' basic attacks, so create distance as the stacks build.

Shaco.build: Build magic resistance and health first against the magic damage from Shaco W Jack In The Box, E Two-Shiv Poison, and R Hallucinate. You need to watch out for the slow from Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison and for Shaco W Jack In The Box, so also consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching.
Shaco.combo: When Shaco Q Deceive is down, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! rolled ahead of time from out of sight. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep him slowed until the root triggers. If Shaco tries to leave the area, end Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early to detonate it.
Shaco.escape: Right after Shaco uses Q Deceive to appear is your window to engage. Immediately use Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage with an ally to catch him before he can escape. If you haven't cleared Shaco W Jack In The Box, start an objective only from a position where you have room to retreat if feared.
Shaco.fight: Right after Shaco Q Deceive is down, close the distance with an ally, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, then catch him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Your early damage is low on your own and you have no ability to escape by yourself, so engage from a distance your allies can follow up from. If you need health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a jungle monster to heal.
Shaco.laning: Keep vision at your jungle entrances to prepare for Shaco's early ganks and invades. Clear Shaco W Jack In The Box around objectives first with a Control Ward or Oracle Lens.
Shaco.phase: Early on, Shaco looks to gain an advantage through ganks and invades, so don't give up kills and maintain vision at your jungle entrances. Buy time into the late game, when Shaco is weaker in solo fights; Nunu & Willump contribute with engages and ally protection.
Shaco.teamfight: When engaging, knock them up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from a distance your allies can follow up from, then follow with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and R Absolute Zero. If there's no opening to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to block Shaco's approach.
Shaco.watch: If Shaco Q Deceive gets him behind you, his empowered basic attack is dangerous, so if you think Shaco is nearby, keep your back to a wall or face toward your allies. Watch out for the fear from Shaco W Jack In The Box in bushes without vision and around objectives. When Shaco R Hallucinate's clone dies, take a step back to avoid the explosion and boxes. When you're low on health, don't pass through jungle or bushes without vision, to avoid being hit by Shaco E Two-Shiv Poison.

Shyvana.build: Build magic resistance first against the main damage from Shyvana W Inferno Aegis, E Molten Burst, and R Dragon's Descent. Also get armor against the physical damage from her basic attacks, and reducing her attack speed can help reduce the damage you take while close to her. Shyvana Q Emberstrike also deals true damage, so resistances alone can't block all of her damage.
Shyvana.combo: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! ahead of time from out of sight to knock Shyvana up, then cast Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times. Follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep her slowed until E's root triggers. If Shyvana is using R Dragon's Descent, wait for her to land before applying crowd control in this order.
Shyvana.escape: The window to go in with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! is when Shyvana R Dragon's Descent is down or after she has landed. Catch her again and retaliate when she returns to human form and loses her bonus health and empowered abilities.
Shyvana.fight: Pressure Shyvana when her Fury bar is empty, and don't start an objective if it's full. If Shyvana engages with R Dragon's Descent, catch her after she lands with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage. If you need healing, carefully use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a minion or monster.
Shyvana.laning: Start rolling the snowball out of sight, far from the lane, to build its speed and size before landing a hit. Pressure Shyvana with ganks and objectives early, before she builds stacks.
Shyvana.phase: In the late game, Shyvana's permanent stacks from P Scalemail make her harder to take down from the same engage angle, so Nunu & Willump should focus on engaging and protecting allies.
Shyvana.teamfight: Spread out your formation so the path of Shyvana R Dragon's Descent and her dragon-form abilities don't hit multiple allies at once. After Shyvana lands, catch her with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and E Snowball Barrage, then follow with Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If your allies can't follow up on an engage, activate R Absolute Zero in front of a carry to block Shyvana's engage.
Shyvana.watch: While Shyvana is flying in with R Dragon's Descent, she's unstoppable, so don't try to interrupt her engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!; hit her after she lands. In dragon form, spread out from allies so Shyvana W Inferno Aegis's explosion and E Molten Burst don't hit multiple people. Shyvana Q Emberstrike and E Molten Burst deal damage based on your max health, so avoid staying in close range and taking repeated hits.

Skarner.build: Build magic resistance first, considering the magic damage from Skarner P Threads of Vibration, W Seismic Bastion, and R Impale. Consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching if there are many slows. Allied damage dealers at high risk of being caught by Skarner R Impale should decide in advance whether to buy Quicksilver Sash or Mercurial Scimitar.
Skarner.combo: When Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! built out of sight and knock him up. Follow with three casts of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep him slowed until the root triggers. If Skarner tries to leave the area of Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero, recast it early to detonate it.
Skarner.escape: Right after Skarner E Ixtal's Impact is down is your window to engage. A stun can't interrupt Skarner R Impale, so don't go in expecting to escape after being suppressed.
Skarner.fight: Close the distance right after you bait Skarner E Ixtal's Impact. In open space, when your allies can follow up, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and catch him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Don't stay in close range and trade damage for long.
Skarner.laning: Look for lanes where allies can follow up instead of trying to secure kills alone. After a gank, roll the Rift Scuttler to build another snowball and look for repeat ganks.
Skarner.phase: In the late game, Skarner gains damage and durability from tank items, so Nunu & Willump should focus on engaging with allies or protecting them.
Skarner.teamfight: Engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only from a distance your allies can follow up from, then follow the knockup with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and R Absolute Zero. If there's no opening to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of an allied carry to block Skarner's approach. Maintain the distance between Skarner and his allies so an allied damage dealer caught by Skarner R Impale isn't dragged too deep.
Skarner.watch: Skarner E Ixtal's Impact charges through terrain and stuns if he hits a wall, so don't stand with your back to one. Skarner R Impale suppresses and drags you away, and a stun can't interrupt it, so stay out of its range and away from the edges of objective pits. After he catches you, Skarner Q Shattered Earth / Upheaval's empowered basic attacks and Skarner P Threads of Vibration damage can follow, so managing your distance is important.

Taliyah.build: Taliyah W Seismic Shove and Taliyah E Unraveled Earth can make it difficult to escape, so prioritize tenacity. Build magic resistance against the magic damage from Taliyah Q Threaded Volley and Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. She also has plenty of slows, so consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching together.
Taliyah.combo: Roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! along a route without Taliyah E Unraveled Earth to knock Taliyah up. While she’s airborne, throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold her with slows until the root triggers. Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero can be walked out of if activated alone, so use it after a knockup or root.
Taliyah.escape: If Taliyah E Unraveled Earth is laid down, don’t roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! through it. The window to engage is after Taliyah W Seismic Shove and Taliyah E Unraveled Earth are down, especially before Taliyah R Weaver's Wall is available again. If only one of Taliyah’s tools is down, she can still escape with the other, so don’t rush your engage.
Taliyah.fight: Taliyah has relatively low magic resistance, so there are opportunities to deal magic damage with Nunu & Willump. However, Nunu & Willump has no abilities to escape on their own, so don’t force your way onto ground covered by Taliyah E Unraveled Earth. Engage from an angle that avoids the stone minefield before Taliyah R Weaver's Wall is available again.
Taliyah.laning: Start rolling the snowball from far away, outside the enemy’s vision, to build speed, and engage within range for your allies to follow up. If Taliyah disappears from the jungle, expect her to use Taliyah P Rock Surfing and Taliyah R Weaver's Wall to intervene in another lane, and fall back early.
Taliyah.phase: In the mid to late game, Nunu & Willump Q Consume provides more sustain and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero becomes more explosive. Even late, your role is to initiate and protect your allies.
Taliyah.teamfight: From within range for your allies to follow up, knock Taliyah up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, then follow with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If Taliyah E Unraveled Earth covers your entry path, take another route. If there’s no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop the enemy from engaging.
Taliyah.watch: Taliyah Q Threaded Volley cannot change direction while casting, so sidestep instead of approaching in a straight line. When engaging with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever!, avoid routes through the stone minefield.

Udyr.build: Build armor first against Udyr. Armor alone can’t block all of the magic damage from Udyr R Wingborne Storm or the mixed damage from Udyr Q Wilding Claw, so be cautious about stacking health alone. If his slows are a problem, consider Mercury's Treads and Unflinching together.
Udyr.combo: After Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s empowered state ends and he uses his movement tool, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! after building it outside vision. Follow with three throws of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with slows until the root triggers. If Udyr tries to leave the area, detonate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early instead of waiting for maximum damage.
Udyr.escape: Udyr E Blazing Stampede is his only movement tool, so the moment right after you make him use it is your window to engage. However, immobilizing effects don’t work while it’s empowered, so catch him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage after the empowered state ends. Conversely, if Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s stun is ready, don’t try to escape on foot alone; save one of these two abilities.
Udyr.fight: After Udyr W Iron Mantle’s shield is removed, press with your allies and don’t give him time to heal. If you’ve already taken a stun from Udyr E Blazing Stampede, use the window when the same target can’t be stunned again for a while to counterattack or retreat. Nunu & Willump’s damage alone is low early, so engage within range for your allies to follow up.
Udyr.laning: When Udyr is out of sight, use vision at key paths and jungle entrances to track his route, and keep your allied laners from pushing too far forward. Look to gain advantages through ganks and objectives rather than competing over farm.
Udyr.phase: Late game, focus on Nunu & Willump’s engage and protecting allies instead of trying to kill Udyr first while he has Udyr W Iron Mantle.
Udyr.teamfight: If Udyr is holding on with defensive items and Udyr W Iron Mantle, don’t focus your efforts on attacking him first; target the weaker enemies behind him. Use Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! to engage when your allies can follow up. If there’s no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop Udyr from approaching. After Udyr E Blazing Stampede’s empowered state ends, catch him with the root from Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
Udyr.watch: Immediately after Udyr activates Udyr E Blazing Stampede, watch out for the stun on his first attack and keep your distance. Udyr Q Wilding Claw and Udyr R Wingborne Storm deal damage based on maximum health, so don’t stay close for an extended fight. Immobilizing effects don’t work while Udyr E Blazing Stampede is empowered, so hit him with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! or Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage after it ends.

Vi.build: Build armor first against Vi, since the main damage from Vi Q Vault Breaker, Vi W Denting Blows, and Vi E Relentless Force is physical. Vi W Denting Blows reduces armor and deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid stacking health alone. If you can handle her basic attacks and attack speed, reducing her attack speed is also effective.
Vi.combo: After Vi Q Vault Breaker is down, knock her up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! rolled from outside vision. Then throw Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage three times and use Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to keep slowing her until the root triggers. If Vi is charging in with Vi R Cease and Desist, start this combo after she lands and her knockup ends.
Vi.escape: The window to engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage is right after you bait out and dodge Vi Q Vault Breaker. If Vi R Cease and Desist has started, don’t try to stop her mid-charge with the snowball; respond after she lands and her knockup ends.
Vi.fight: Vi W Denting Blows becomes more punishing the more she hits the same target in a row, so avoid extended trades and create distance. Immediately after dodging or baiting out Vi Q Vault Breaker, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! from within range for your allies to attack with you. If you need health, use Nunu & Willump Q Consume on a minion or monster to heal.
Vi.laning: Start rolling the snowball far from the lane, outside vision, to build its speed and size. If Vi has just used an ability on a minion to activate her shield, start the fight after the shield is removed.
Vi.phase: In the mid to late game, Q Consume provides more sustain and R Absolute Zero becomes more explosive. Even late, you handle engages and protect allies. The information provided isn’t enough to determine which champion has the advantage at each stage of the game.
Vi.teamfight: Engage on the enemy back line with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! only when your allies can follow up. While Vi R Cease and Desist is ready, make sure your allied backline carries don’t wander out of vision alone. If there’s no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your carry to stop Vi from approaching. If Vi is charging in with Vi R Cease and Desist, save forced movement and use it after she lands.
Vi.watch: A fully charged Vi Q Vault Breaker deals more damage and closes the gap with a dash. When you see her charging, move backward or to the side to dodge. Forced movement can’t stop Vi R Cease and Desist while she’s charging in, so save Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! until she lands and her knockup ends.

Viego.build: Build armor first against the physical damage from Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King and Viego R Heartbreaker. Armor can’t block the magic damage from Viego W Spectral Maw. If the duel drags on, get Grievous Wounds to counter the healing from Viego P Sovereign's Domination and Viego Q Blade of the Ruined King.
Viego.combo: Before Viego R Heartbreaker is available again, roll Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! outside vision to build speed, then knock Viego up. Follow with three throws of Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage, then activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero to hold him with slows until the root triggers. If Viego tries to escape, end Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero early to detonate it.
Viego.escape: If you engage just because Viego W Spectral Maw is down, Viego can escape with Viego R Heartbreaker. Look to engage before Viego R Heartbreaker is available again, when Viego W Spectral Maw is also down, using Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage.
Viego.fight: Nunu & Willump doesn’t have enough damage to secure kills alone, so engage when your allies can follow up. If Viego W Spectral Maw is down and Viego R Heartbreaker isn’t available again yet, knock him up with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and catch him with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage. Back away without giving up a kill if you can’t win a skirmish.
Viego.laning: When black mist from Viego E Harrowed Path appears on terrain, don’t push the lane in that direction; take a route around it. After a gank, you can roll the Rift Scuttler to build the snowball up again and look for another gank.
Viego.phase: Even late, Nunu & Willump contributes through engaging and protecting allies. Treat the moment Viego’s possession ends and he returns to his original body as a chance to counterattack.
Viego.teamfight: From within range for your allies to follow up, engage with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! and hold the enemy with Nunu & Willump E Snowball Barrage and Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero. If there’s no good angle to engage, activate Nunu & Willump R Absolute Zero in front of your allied carry to stop Viego from engaging. If an ally is killed, fight away from the spot or lock Viego down with crowd control so he can’t interact with the wraith left there.
Viego.watch: The longer Viego charges Viego W Spectral Maw, the longer its stun lasts, so sidestep when you see him charging and interrupt it with Nunu & Willump W Biggest Snowball Ever! If Viego E Harrowed Path appears on terrain, avoid that route, and fall back when health is low to avoid becoming a target for Viego R Heartbreaker.
